clue.text: Depending on oxygen, agents carry windbag around

indicators.note: around turns the whole assembled string the other way
the agents carry the windbag, holding it inside them

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of agents
a bore is a tedious talker, a windbag

explanation.surface: Spies lug a tiresome talker about while relying on oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windbag' suggests a wind instrument or bagpipe, but it is a tedious talker; 'around' turns the whole container result, not just the agents.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic processes or organisms need free oxygen to function, so they depend on it.

clue.text: Don amuses, clowning about

indicators.note: clowning about suggests the letters of amuses fooling around into a new order

explanation.surface: A university teacher entertains people by playing the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clowning about' rearranges AMUSES. 'Don' looks like a university lecturer but is the verb meaning to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: To don a garment or a manner is to put it on, which is one sense of the verb assume.

clue.text: Stroll before river rose

parts.note: to stroll or wander is to ramble

explanation.surface: A walk taken before reaching the river at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the past tense of rise, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a climbing rose variety with long trailing stems.

clue.text: Crude and hurtful remark to someone born in spring

parts.note: a barb is a cutting, hurtful remark
an Arian is someone born under Aries, the star sign covering late March to April

explanation.surface: A rude, wounding comment aimed at a person with a spring birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbarian is uncivilised and coarse, so the word serves as an adjective meaning crude.

clue.text: Bed with single plant a shrub with berries

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
single means one
the aster is a daisy-like garden plant

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction: a bed holding one plant and one berry bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotoneaster is a genus of shrubs grown for their bright red berries.

clue.text: Pong certain to be spread about by this bone

parts.note: pong and hum are both British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: spread about suggests the letters of the synonym being scattered into a new order

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: A bad smell is sure to be scattered around by a particular bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be spread about' rearranges SURE into ERUS. 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm.

clue.text: Layer of humus encourages new heads

indicators.note: heads indicates taking the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A layer of rich soil helps fresh shoots come through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' reads as a stratum of soil but is the bird that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen lays eggs, so in crossword terms she is a layer.

clue.text: Chap picked up an unexpected windfall

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word an is read upwards, that is backwards

explanation.surface: A fellow came across a sudden stroke of good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests a homophone, but in a down answer it lifts AN to read NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna from heaven is a proverbial unexpected benefit or windfall.

clue.text: Remarkable miracle required to make a recovery like this

definitions.note: reclaim is here a noun, as in beyond reclaim

indicators.note: remarkable can be read as re-markable, the letters of miracle marked out afresh

explanation.surface: Only an astonishing miracle could bring about a recovery of this sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkable' rearranges MIRACLE; 'required to make a' and 'like this' are link words. RECLAIM is the noun, as in 'beyond reclaim'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, reclaim means the act of getting something back, a recovery.

clue.text: Tumultuous southern river I had entered

indicators.note: entered means the contraction goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
I had contracts to I'd, giving ID

explanation.surface: A rough river in the south that I had paddled into.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TRENT is a long river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and harsh, which fits something noisy and tumultuous.

clue.text: Helpful chap at marina's sacked

indicators.note: sacked, as a city is ravaged, suggests the letters being thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A kindly man at the harbour has lost his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges AT MARINAS, the S of the possessive counting as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable of the Good Samaritan, the word names anyone who helps a stranger in need.

clue.text: Finish off bun? One finishes off cake — it's more appealing

indicators.note: finish off picks the final letter of bun

parts.note: an icer is a person who ices, completing a cake

explanation.surface: Polishing off a bun and then the iced cake is more pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer means pleasanter, more agreeable and therefore more appealing.

clue.text: Island producing whisky, foremost among alcohols

parts.note: malt is short for malt whisky

indicators.note: foremost among takes the first letter of alcohols

explanation.surface: An island makes whisky, the best of all spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is a Mediterranean island nation south of Sicily.

clue.text: Ann's a lady relocated to the old country

indicators.note: relocated suggests the letters moving to new positions

explanation.surface: Ann, a woman, has moved away from her former homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocated' rearranges ANNS A LADY; the apostrophe's S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyasaland was the colonial name of Malawi until 1964, so it is a country of the past.

clue.text: Piece to your taste?

parts.note: a piece is a play, and one whose title promises it suits you is a Shakespeare comedy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests a slice of food, but it means a stage work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shakespeare comedy's title literally means however you prefer, suited to your taste.

clue.text: Crew member, excessively large, expanded

definitions.meaning: a junior rank of sailor in a ship's crew
outsize is abbreviated OS, the same letters that abbreviate this rank, so writing OS out in full gives it

explanation.surface: A sailor, grown far too big, has got bigger still.
explanation.walkthrough: OS stands both for outsize (clothing sizes) and for the naval rank; 'expanded' asks for the abbreviation spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lowest rating of seaman in the Royal Navy, a member of a ship's crew.

clue.text: Clobber I'd cast? Yes!

indicators.note: clobber, to bash about, signals the letters of I'd cast yes being knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A stripper delightedly admits to having thrown off her clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is British slang for clothes as well as the anagram signal, so the whole clue is the stripper's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecdysiast is a striptease artist, someone who casts off her clothes.

clue.text: Bill and Paul, having company, quietly sinking a little port

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: sinking a little means the letter for quiet drops one place lower in this down light

parts.note: taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Two men and some friends quietly scuttle a boat in a small harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinking a little' moves the P of PAULCO one place down, giving APULCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a Pacific port and resort city in Mexico.

clue.text: Ministers messing about left out sweet

parts.note: the cabinet is the body of senior government ministers

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is removed

parts.note: puddling means dabbling or messing about

explanation.surface: Government ministers fooling around have ignored the left wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabinet pudding is a steamed dessert of sponge, dried fruit and custard, a British sweet.

clue.text: City raised objection to cleaning facility

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: but is a word of objection, as in no buts

explanation.surface: A town protested about its washing amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a Roman spa city in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathtub is a tub for washing oneself in, a facility for getting clean.

clue.text: Opening numbers sound tremulous, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to trill is to sound with a quavering, tremulous voice

explanation.surface: The opening songs are delivered in a mostly shaky voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is one of the openings of the nose.

clue.text: Loud insect circling tree

indicators.note: circling means the insect goes round the tree

parts.note: a fly is an insect
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A noisy bug flies round and round a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud is used of colours or clothes that are showy and gaudy, which is what flashy means.

clue.text: Holding nothing back break into musical work, a medley

indicators.note: holding means the reversed string contains the zero
back turns the following verb and the opus abbreviation round to read in reverse

parts.note: to irrupt is to burst or break into
OP is short for opus, a numbered musical work
O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: Unrestrained, someone bursts into a composition that turns out to be a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IRRUPT plus OP into POTPURRI, and 'Holding' puts the O for nothing inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a mixed collection, used of music for a medley of tunes.

clue.text: Letter addressed to Welsh girl? It's nameless

parts.note: O is the old vocative used when addressing someone, as in O Megan

indicators.note: nameless means the abbreviation for name, N, is removed from the girl

parts.note: Megan is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A note sent to a Welsh lass is anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Fibre and endless seasoning one's eaten

indicators.note: eaten means one piece is swallowed inside the other
endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: salt is a seasoning
one's is I's, giving IS

explanation.surface: Roughage and unlimited salt have been consumed by one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a strong plant fibre used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Not inflexible — still, it helps a bit

indicators.note: a bit signals the answer is a small piece taken from the words still it helps

explanation.surface: Being supple is still something of an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and flexible, so not stiff or inflexible.

clue.text: Reference book man's brought into the house

indicators.note: brought into means the man's piece is placed inside the house

parts.note: Taurus is one of the twelve houses or signs of the zodiac
man's read as he is, contracted to he's

explanation.surface: A guidebook that some fellow has carried into the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the house' looks like a home, but astrology calls each zodiac sign a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms.

clue.text: Unruly youngster used to make hay

definitions.meaning: a teddy boy, a rebellious 1950s British youth
to turn and spread mown grass so it dries into hay

explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits, seen as delinquents.
explanation.definitionFit: Ted is short for teddy boy, and also a verb meaning to spread grass for drying.

clue.text: Safely ensconced among directors

definitions.meaning: aboard a ship or vehicle, securely settled in
serving as a member of a company's board of directors

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both aboard a vessel and serving on a board of directors.

clue.text: To match perfectly

parts.note: to tally is to correspond or match

explanation.surface: Things that agree in every detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally means completely or entirely, which is a sense of perfectly.
